summary: ```# Quick Start Second Edition! How to Make a Maid Outfit? p04: Making Ruffles ## Introduction In this section, we will explore how to create a maid outfit, specifically focusing on the process of making ruffles. This tutorial will guide you through various steps, including particle diameter adjustments, simulation settings, and sewing techniques. ## Panel Activation To begin, press **SHIFT + W** to show all the panels. You will notice the panels that were anti-activated before activation. After activation, observe that there was no constraint when anti-activated previously, leading to an intersection with the panels inside. ## Particle Diameter Adjustment First, we can see that the particle diameter of the inner panel is relatively small, which is **8**. The particle diameter of the outer panel is **20**. The network gap is far from enough. Therefore, let's reduce the particle diameter of the outer panel to **10** and the conflict thickness to **1**. ## Shoulder Strap Configuration Next, select all the shoulder straps and set their levels to **1** in the attribute editor. The default level of the panel is **0**. Once we start the simulation, the panels with higher levels will automatically be worn on the outside of the panels with lower levels. After the shoulder strap part is worn out, press **CTRL + A** to select all the panels, activate the simulation, and allow them to interact with each other. Once the simulation is done, press **CTRL + A** again to select all the panels and return their levels to **0**. Next, press the grid line again to simulate and freeze these panels. ## Joint Edge Creation Now, let's focus on the details of the shoulder strap part. The joint edge can be generated by sewing a longer panel on a shorter panel, which will create the joint edge. Additionally, the joint edge can also be created by sewing a shorter panel on another shorter panel. Using the rectangle tool, in the 2D window, click and drag to draw a rectangle that is longer than before. Use the line powder tool to sew the sides of the two panels together. After that, select the entire joint edge panel using the adjustment panel tool and press **CTRL + D**. Click in the 2D window to arrange, and press the control key to simulate and sew the joint edge. ## Particle Diameter and Fold Adjustment Since our current panel has a larger particle diameter, its fold is not very detailed. We will reduce the particle diameter and then copy and paste this pair of joint edges. Select the level in the 3D space and turn it over to the back. Drag these two panels in the 3D space and take the other group of the back panel. The joint edge will automatically generate a seam line. ## Seam Line Creation While in the back of the virtual model, you can select the final panel in the 3D window and arrange them in the 2D window to create a seam line. Alternatively, you can directly use the 3D sewing tool in the 3D window. Click on the joint edge and then click on the shoulder strap. Press the control key to start the simulation. For the belt, we will use the free sewing tool to sew the bottom side of the contract. Create the first section of the sewing line, and when your mouse stops at the previous shoulder strap of this set of sewing lines, you can find another sewing line. Start from the end of this sewing line to create the other half. ## Side Contract Adjustment For the side contract, click from the inside point to create the first set of sewing lines, then find the corresponding position on the belt and sew outward, ensuring the direction is correct. The contract is seen from the front on one side and from the back on the other side. After using the free sewing tool, we will adjust the side of the contract. First, drag the top point to the outside while pressing the **Shift** key to move in the direction of the reference lines. You can enter specific numbers using the right mouse button during this operation. ## Chest Pattern Creation Next, we will make the padded pattern on the chest. Since there is no cut on this line on the whole belt pattern, we will use the writing sewing line tool. The mark near the sewing line is the starting point, with the distance being the end point. Select the sewing line, right-click, and select the end point of the sewing line, then click to add a point. Switch to the adjustment pattern tool, and you will see a straight line point. Draw a rectangle that is almost wide according to the position of this straight line point and set the height at will. You can refer to the pink guide line during the adjustment. ## Symmetry and Side Line Adjustment After selecting the line in front, right-click and select symmetry to open the edit sewing line function. This pattern is symmetrical; sewing one side will automatically generate a sewing line on the other side. For the side line, since there is no cut, we will again use the free sewing tool. Select the part of the cloth and go to the shoulder strap to click the starting point and then the endpoint. After placing it in the 3D space, press the control key to simulate it. After the simulation, activate all the cold plates next to it to simulate once again. ## Final Adjustments After the simulation, you will see that the position of the shoulder strap and seam line is deformed. Adjust the width of the seam line as necessary. The width of the bottom plate is correct, but the shoulder strap may need adjustments in the middle part. Move the side point out a little and stretch the plate longer as required. Use the editing sewing line tool to drag the edge of the sewing line to the corresponding blue length support point. Repeat this step until the shoulder strap reaches the desired height. Adjust the width of the shoulder strap as needed and ensure to modify the side of the plate. If there are wrinkles on the chest, you can adjust the widened part inward. Finally, move the rest of the shoulder strap and the seam line together to simulate. For the frozen plate, you can choose to activate or move it back to its original state. After the simulation is complete, select all the plates and freeze them together. ```
